title: Investigating the feasibility of motorcycle autonomous emergency braking (MAEB): Design criteria for new experiments to field test automatic braking
author: Lucci, Marra, et al.
materials:
Since grating participants’ safety is the main concern and an ethical duty in research involving human beings [15,16], the design of the experiment in the approach of the participant to the intervention of AB must find a compromise between the optimal design [20] and safety. Therefore, before testing an unexpected intervention of AB the participant experiences expected interventions with levels of deceleration considered safe in the literature (at present, up to 2 m/s2
[2,3]). Even if it could be a source of bias due to learning effects, this lets the participant have a safe familiarization with AB before testing new decelerations and maneuvers. Furthermore, measures of these declared AB interventions can be used to compare the rider's response with those responses during the unexpected interventions of the test.

steps.title: Inform participant and complete paperwork
steps.instruction: Provide the participant with all test information, verify that all consent and eligibility forms are signed, and check that all required protective equipment is inspected and correctly fitted.

steps.title: Show vehicle, controls and demonstration
steps.instruction: Present the test motorcycle, explain its special AB controls, and give a brief demonstration of riding on the test track, including how to approach the track and perform the required maneuvers.

steps.title: Warm‑up familiarization on track
steps.instruction: Allow the participant a 10–15 minute warm‑up to become familiar with the motorcycle, the track layout and all maneuvers that will be used in the test.

steps.title: Collect baseline manual braking data
steps.instruction: At an initial speed of 40–45 km/h the participant performs three manual hard‑braking stops corresponding to approximately 30 %, 50 % and 90 % of his/her maximum achievable deceleration with the test vehicle.

steps.title: Familiarize with declared AB activations
steps.instruction: At a speed of 40–50 km/h the participant tests declared AB activations at the planned deceleration levels in straight‑line riding (duration ≈ 5 min).

steps.title: Perform safe expected AB interventions
steps.instruction: Before any unexpected activation, let the participant experience expected AB interventions with deceleration values considered safe in the literature (up to 2 m/s²) to ensure a safe familiarisation.

steps.title: Explain unexpected AB trial parameters
steps.instruction: The investigator explains the upcoming unexpected activations, describing the intended deceleration, jerk and maneuver, and asks the rider whether any maneuver should be excluded from the trial.

steps.title: First unexpected AB test session
steps.instruction: Trigger the AB system in unexpected conditions at the lowest deceleration level, using a pseudorandom schedule of activation points along the track; the participant may request a single declared activation to be included or excluded before the session starts.

substeps.instruction: Activate AB at each pseudorandom point (Number of Activations × 100 s).
After each trial, obtain participant feedback before proceeding to the next activation.

steps.title: Break and brief questionnaire
steps.instruction: Give the participant a short rest and have them complete a brief questionnaire on the demands of interacting with the system.

steps.title: Further AB test sessions
steps.instruction: Repeat the unexpected‑activation procedure with higher deceleration or jerk levels, following the same pseudorandom schedule; the participant may again request a declared activation to be included or excluded.

substeps.instruction: End with a break and a brief questionnaire.

steps.title: Final questionnaire and interview
steps.instruction: Have the participant complete a final questionnaire covering the entire test and the MAEB system; optionally record an interview (duration ≈ 15 min).

steps.title: Limit total test duration
steps.instruction: Ensure that the whole testing session, including all phases and breaks, does not exceed two hours to avoid excessive fatigue and psychological overload.
